description: A user needs a clean controller-side rights request and, if necessary, a competent DPA complaint.
entry_signals: No clear systemic pattern; no cross-border coordination need; no regulator-delay story yet.
primary_goal: Get a real answer, correction, deletion, or review for the complainant.
exit_signal: Controller reply received or DPA complaint filed with a usable chronology.
not_for: Media-first campaigning or broad political pressure before the facts are documented.

description: The same GDPR failure appears repeatable across users or products and may need watchdog or coalition support.
entry_signals: Repeat-pattern evidence; consent or profiling abuse; adtech or dark-pattern concerns.
primary_goal: Move from one complainant to a credible systemic narrative with supporting evidence.
exit_signal: Issue framed as a repeat-pattern case with external support or a stronger complaint package.
not_for: Thin one-off personal disputes with no pattern signal.

description: The complaint turns on one-stop-shop dynamics, lead-authority questions, or several complainants across borders.
entry_signals: Likely lead DPA matters; several countries or complainants are involved; controller establishment is relevant.
primary_goal: Coordinate facts cleanly and choose the right cross-border framing before escalation widens.
exit_signal: Shared chronology agreed and cross-border route clarified.
not_for: Single-country personal complaints with no establishment or OSS issue.

description: The issue is no longer only the company conduct but the quality, pace, or seriousness of enforcement.
entry_signals: DPA complaint filed; regulator silence or visible under-action; pressure for accountability needed.
primary_goal: Document delay, follow up cleanly, and escalate through watchdog, media, or political oversight only when the chronology supports it.
exit_signal: A regulator reply, procedural step, or credible public-interest escalation path exists.
not_for: Initial controller contact where no complaint has been filed yet.
